candidates: When adding `textDecoration: 'underline'` as the base style to a shared Link/anchor component that also has button-like variants (e.g., the `isButton` variant in `code/core/src/components/components/typography/link/link.tsx`), check every variant branch and explicitly set `textDecoration: 'none'` on any that are intended to look like buttons rather than inline text links, to prevent unintended visual regression on call sites such as `RefBlocks.tsx` and `Description.tsx`.

When adding an inline comment to justify a `textDecoration: 'underline'` rule for WCAG accessibility compliance, cite the specific failure technique in addition to the success criterion: `// Ensure WCAG Level A compliance (SC 1.4.1), see https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/F73`.

Do not add WCAG SC 1.4.1 justification comments to `textDecoration: 'none'` overrides on button-styled components or button-like Link variants (e.g., `Button.tsx`, the `isButton` branch in `link.tsx`); these overrides are self-evident and the WCAG success criterion for distinguishing links from surrounding text does not apply to button-styled elements.

Use `textUnderlineOffset: '0.2em'` (not `0.11em`) when setting the underline offset on link typography in this project's components (`DocumentWrapper.tsx`, `A.tsx`, `link.tsx`, `DocsPage.tsx`); this value has been validated through browser testing to render more comfortably.
